answer: A wharf can bind each agent to one numbered berth plus a ballast ledger. Each epoch the seat lands a fist-sized stone from a licensed quarry, shot on the berth plate; an XRF reads its zirconium-to-strontium ratio, which shifts between blast faces, so old samples and copied images fail. Peers log liveness too: the sparrow flock feeds only where someone works, and a falcon stoop scatters it, so idle berths stand out. A fake identity costs a quarry face, haulage and a person-day at the wharf per epoch, linear and unrentable; two seats on one face collide on spectra and forfeit both bonds.
